1. Access the principal's client briefing records and locate the Acme Q1 market data information.

6. Send the email.
7. Confirm completion to the principal.

- Northeast: +9% YoY (steady—no notable competitive shifts)
  [Source: Acme syndicated dashboard]

- Mar: 34% of category SOV (steady leadership—recommend hold spend in Q2)

- Jan: +22% during MLK weekend reset (outperformed planned +15%)
- Feb: +18% during Super Bowl window (met plan)
  [Source: Acme syndicated dashboard]

Best regards,
Daniel Park
Pinecrest Strategy Group"}

arguments.subject: Acme Q1 Market Data Information
arguments.body:
Hi Priya,

Please find below the requested market data for Acme Q1. If you have any questions or need further detail, feel free to reach out at any time.

---
Acme Q1 Key Market Data Highlights:

1. Category Share Protein Bars: 
- Jan: 18.4% (up 60bps QoQ—driven by club channel reset)
- Feb: 18.6% (share holding—Verdant flat—see analyst note)
- Mar: 18.9% (share continuing to grow—Verdant flat-to-down)
  [Source: Nielsen scanner]

2. Retail Velocity (Protein Bar SKU, US total):
- Jan: 4.7 units/store/week (steady—top-3 SKU in category)
- Feb: 4.9 units/store/week (uptick—Q1 promo driving trial)
- Mar: 5.1 units/store/week (best Q1 reading—momentum continues)
  [Source: IRI scan]

3. Regional Momentum:
- Southeast: +12% YoY (strongest region—pull-through from Walmart reset)
- West: +8% YoY (below plan—competitive pressure from private label)
- Northeast: +9% YoY (steady—no notable competitive shifts)
  [Source: Acme syndicated dashboard]

4. Share of Voice (Digital, US total):
- Feb: 33% of category SOV (leading category—Verdant at 24%)
- Mar: 34% of category SOV (steady leadership—recommend hold spend in Q2)
  [Source: Pathmatics digital ad scrape]

5. Promo Lift:
- Jan: +22% during MLK weekend reset (outperformed planned +15%)
- Feb: +18% during Super Bowl window (met plan)
  [Source: Acme syndicated dashboard]

Let me know if you require the full data file or wish to discuss any of these insights further.

Best regards,
Daniel Park
Pinecrest Strategy Group
